content.content:
A later revision of the interpreter changes both boxes on it.
The box in \secref{static-arg-inference} said that, where no argument's type is
the narrowest, the interpreter ``binds a type parameter that is the whole type
of parameters to the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments'
run-time types that the bounds permit'', the bound only where the bound is that
supertype; it now says that the interpreter gives such a type parameter its
bound, \TYP{Any} if it has none, and does the same where the arguments that fix
a type parameter inside other types have several minimal common supertypes,
except a type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter and one
declared with several bounds that the interpreter cannot meet, which it binds as
before to the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments' run-time
types, a call that fixes one of the second kind failing where there is none;
that when it chooses among declarations it passes over a declaration with
static parameters whose arguments have several minimal common supertypes in
favour of another applicable without coercion; and that it instantiates at
\TYP{BottomType} a type parameter that an argument bounds only from above.
The box after the list said that ``The interpreter erases a type parameter that
nothing at a call fixes, of a function, to \TYP{BottomType}''; it now says that
the interpreter instantiates such a type parameter at its bound, and one whose
bound mentions other static parameters at that bound with their instances,
except a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
arguments fix mentions, which it instantiates at the arguments' type, and
names the type parameters it still erases: one declared with several bounds
that it cannot meet, one whose bound mentions the type parameter itself, a big
operator's that a reduction or a comprehension does not write, and one that
only the result of a function expression without a declared return type
fixes.
\item[Rationale] This change does not follow from route~A.
The revival decided on 26~September 2026 that a generic call over two different
integer types infers the narrowest type that both coerce into, by a rule
written into this chapter; on 27~September 2026 that the compiled type checker
infers static arguments with coercion and keeps the expected type at a call
written as \EXP{f(x)}, with a retry without it so that a coercion of the result
still applies, and that the chapter is written with it; and on 28~September
2026 that a coercion makes a call possible and never changes which declaration
runs when one is applicable without it, the declaration chosen being then
instantiated by that rule, that a numeral whose conversions tie is read as a
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, and that a \KWD{nat} parameter used as a value converts to
\EXP{\mathbb{Z}32} as a numeral does.
\chapref{multiple-dispatch}, \secref{idn-ref} and \secref{dotted-method-calls}
said that static arguments are inferred as \chapref{type-inference} describes,
and it described nothing; once the compiled type checker infers them by a rule
the text does not state, the text and the implementation disagree, so the
chapter states the rule the checker was built to, and the effect below lists
where the checker departs from it.
The bound in place of the union is the rule by which the dispatcher of the type
group's paper of 2019 instantiates a type parameter that the arguments do not
fix, the intersection of its upper bounds, never \TYP{BottomType}; the team
had assumed the union of the lower bounds, of which the authors write ``we were
unable to complete the proofs of correctness'' (Park, Hong, Steele and Ryu,
``Polymorphic Symmetric Multiple Dispatch with Variance'', POPL 2019,
Section~5.4).
The paper gives no algorithm for static inference and asks of it only that it
never instantiate at \TYP{BottomType}; its one example of a static call is
typed at the union of its arguments' types.
The revival decided on 29~September 2026 to take the paper's rule for static
inference as well, which the paper allows and does not require.
The same rule gives a type parameter that neither an argument nor the expected
type fixes the intersection of its upper bounds: the paper's solving step
``never instantiates method type parameters with Bottom'' (Section~5.2), which
answers the question the Working Draft's own note asks, whether type inference
may infer \TYP{BottomType} for a static parameter.
The reasoning for that item, and for the order in which the compiled type
checker tries a call, is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-instance-bound/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
The revival's decision of 29~September 2026 provided that the interpreter
follow the same rule where it instantiates a declaration, from the run-time
types of the arguments; it has no static return type to add to the bound.
It departs from the rule for the type parameters that the two boxes name,
four kinds by decision and the others as defects.
By decision, a type parameter whose bound mentions the type parameter itself
keeps \TYP{BottomType}: it has no bound to take before its own instance is
known, the paper's calculus admits no type parameter of a method in an upper
bound (p.~11:11), and the revival has not yet decided that case.
By decision, so does a big operator's static parameter that a reduction or a
comprehension does not write: it is the element type of the reduction, which
this chapter does not yet describe, and from \TYP{BottomType} the interpreter's
library builds a comprehension's collection at the type of its elements, where
from the bound it would build it at the bound.
By decision, a type parameter that only the bound of a type parameter that the
arguments fix mentions takes the arguments' type: the interpreter has no
expected type to fix it, and the library's operator that appends two covariant
collections builds its result at such a type parameter, which at its bound
would be \TYP{Any}.
By decision, a lone type parameter whose bound mentions a static parameter,
itself or another, keeps the narrowest named common supertype of the arguments
rather than its bound: the interpreter cannot evaluate such a bound before the
instances are known, and keeping the candidates it had leaves unchanged the
case of a type parameter whose bound mentions itself, which the revival has
not yet decided.
As defects, each gated by an expected failure of the revival's tests, the
interpreter erases to \TYP{BottomType} a type parameter declared with several
bounds that it cannot meet, having no intersection type, a type parameter that
only the result of a function expression without a declared return type fixes,
since it gives that result the type \TYP{BottomType}, and a type parameter that
an argument bounds only from above, since it takes the lower end of the
interval that the arguments give the type parameter.

A strided slice of a string, which raised on the base, now answers the specification's set; the first pass's head answered wrong characters (`"abcde"`, section 13), which no landed tree carries. This holds for an explicit strided range and for the implicit forms `a::c` and `::c`. For the implicit `:b:c`, String answers what List and the arrays answer, the range library's completion anchored at the range's right end (`"abcdef"[:3:2]` is `bd`, through `RightScalarRange`, `Library/RangeInternals.fss:655-690`), where ranges.tex, section "Ranges", treats `:b:c` as `l:b:c`, here `ac`; the base raised. That is row 609, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXSubscriptImplicitStridedRange.fss`, and its repair is the range library's (the gather, the second judgement's correction; `SKEPTIC.md`, second judgement, sections 4 and 5). String's default CASE_INSENSITIVE_CMP, which died on the base, now answers by the library's contract. The edit's probe printed the same seven lines at `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`. No program of the corpora reads `.left` or `.right` of a CatString, writes such a SubString, or slices a string with a strided range (`grep` of `ProjectFortress/tests`, `demos` and the `*_tests` corpora; the six team string tests pass, section 13). Unchanged and asserted: halves through `splitWithOffsets`, `asFlatString`, `asExprString`, `asDebugString`, comparisons, membership, compact substrings, `reverse`, `print` and `println` through a WriteStream, the statistics and their getters, rebalancing. These five are the record's stop "a repair that changes a value walk prints"; they are listed for Pavol (section 12).
- Strided string slices now answer the specification's set, by List's device at String's `opr[r0]` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4170-4177`; ranges.tex, section "Ranges"). The base raised (`Library/FlatString.fss:64`), and the first pass's head answered wrong characters. This holds for an explicit strided range and for the implicit forms `a::c` and `::c`. For the implicit `:b:c`, String answers what List and the arrays answer, the range library's completion anchored at the range's right end (`"abcdef"[:3:2]` is `bd`, through `RightScalarRange`, `Library/RangeInternals.fss:655-690`), where ranges.tex, section "Ranges", treats `:b:c` as `l:b:c`, here `ac`; the base raised. That is row 609, gated by `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXSubscriptImplicitStridedRange.fss`, and its repair is the range library's (the gather, the second judgement's correction; `SKEPTIC.md`, second judgement, sections 4 and 5).
6. **The main component's clauses only.** Considered: every clause of the program, as the text and the checker read them; every clause against extenders of its own component. Both refuse the library's `Reflect` (section 5), and the first also four team tests; both meet this rung's stops and turn the gate red. Reading the main component's clauses repairs row 551 for the main component only, and leaves the library's clauses to Pavol. Row 551's scope, "within one" component, is any component: its program inside another component of the user's program still loads under walk and dispatches to `f(S)` (the skeptic's `SkNonMain551`), and so does an object expression that extends both closed traits (`SkObjExpr551`), so row 551 stays open for both, the second also row 597 (the gather, correction 1; `SKEPTIC.md` sections 3 and 8). A third scope, every component outside the library, would refuse neither `Reflect` nor the team tests and close the first case; it was not considered here and goes to Pavol.

content.content:
**What batch 7b built.** Its lift reads a generic declaration beside a plain one on their declared domains. Where neither domain lies inside the other, it asks that declarations below both cover the overlap (`validOnDeclaredDomains`, `OverloadedFunction.java:693-722`). The overlap was read by instantiating the generic at its bounds. That holds every value of the generic only when each type parameter is a whole parameter type with at most one bound naming no static parameter, and any other generic was refused (`genericOverlapCovered` at the base, `:736-763`).

**What the edit reads.** Each parameter of the generic is read as the types whose intersection holds every value it takes in any instance (`:728-778`):
- a type parameter as its bounds that name no static parameter, or `Any` when none is left;
- a type that mentions a static parameter as `Any`;
- any other type as itself.

A non-type static parameter is no longer a reason to refuse, and a single parameter of tuple type is read by its elements.

**How it is cut.** `overlapCoveredBy` (`:834-903`) takes these sets. `intersectionPieces` (`:917-976`) cuts the intersection of any number of types by the `comprises` clauses, as `overlapPieces` cuts two. For two types it is `overlapPieces` itself, so every pair of plain declarations, and every generic of the shape read before, is read exactly as before.

**Why it is sound.** Each reading holds every value of the generic; it is an over-approximation where a parameter mentions a static parameter. A cover still has to lie inside an instance of the generic (`instanceHolding`), so the reading only loads sets whose overlap is covered.

Programs in `tmp/rung-walk-load-check/p552/`, each run with `bin/fortress P.fss` on the edit and in the base copy:

| program | base | edit |
|---|---|---|
| `NatParam` (`w[\T extends Aa, nat n\](x: T, y: ZZ32)`, a plain pair and their meet) | refused, "with generic type, ..." | `meet`, `bothAny` |
| `InsideTrait` (`w[\T\](x: Box[\T\], y: ZZ32)` beside `w(x: IntBox, y: Any)`, meet on `IntBox, ZZ32`) | refused | `meet`, `generic`, `intBoxAny` |
| `FBoundTrait` (`w[\T extends Ord[\T\]\](x: T, y: ZZ32)`, traits `Pt`, `Qt`) | refused | `meet`, `generic`, `ptAny` |
| `InsideTraitUncovered` (no meet) | refused | refused, same message |
| `TwoBoundsUncovered` (no meet) | refused | refused, same message |
| `TwoBoundsExcluding` (overlap empty by an exclusion) | `generic`, `cAny` | the same |

The sets that now load are those of the table's first three rows and of `GenericBesidePlainTwoBounds`. With an object instead of a trait in the type parameter's place (`InsideType`, `FBound`), the base already loads them. Its parameter-by-parameter check finds `Box[\T\]` and the object excluding through instantiation exclusion before the lift is reached.

component XXXSubscriptImplicitStridedRange
import List.{...}
export Executable

(* An implicit range :b:c used as a subscript is completed as l:b:c from the lower bound l of the subscripted axis (row 609); Specification/basic/expressions/ranges.tex, section "Ranges". *)

run() = do
    arr: ZZ32[6] = [10 11 12 13 14 15]
    l = <|"a","b","c","d","e","f"|>
    assert((arr[:3:2])[0], 10, "ranges.tex, section \"Ranges\": the implicit range :3:2 is treated as l:3:2, here 0:3:2, so the first element of arr[:3:2] is arr[0], 10")
    assert(|arr[:3:2]|, 2, "ranges.tex, section \"Ranges\": arr[:3:2] is arr[0:3:2], two elements")
    assert(l[:3:2], <|"a","c"|>, "ranges.tex, section \"Ranges\": the implicit range :3:2 is treated as 0:3:2, so the list's [:3:2] is a and c")
    assert("abcdef"[:3:2], "ac", "ranges.tex, section \"Ranges\": the implicit range :3:2 is treated as 0:3:2, so \"abcdef\"[:3:2] is ac")
    println("PASS")
  end

end
\begin{itemize}
\item The range \EXP{a\COLONOP{}b} is the set of $n=\max(0,b-a+1)$ integers $\{a, a+1, a+2, \ldots, b-2, b-1, b\}$.
This is a \emph{nonstrided} range.
If \VAR{a} and \VAR{b} are both static expressions
(described in \secref{static-expr}),
then it is a \emph{static range} of type \EXP{\TYP{StaticRange}\llbracket{}a,n,1\rrbracket}
and therefore also a \emph{range of static size} of type \EXP{\TYP{RangeOfStaticSize}\llbracket{}n\rrbracket}.

\item The range \EXP{a\COLONOP{}b\COLONOP{}c} is
the set of $n=\max\left(0, \left\lfloor {b-a+c \over c} \right\rfloor \right)$ integers
$\{a, a+c, a+2c, \ldots, a + \left\lfloor {b-a \over c} \right\rfloor c\}$,
unless $c$ is zero, in which case it throws an exception.
(If $c$ is a static expression, then it is a static error if $c$ is zero.)
This is a \emph{strided} range.
If \VAR{a}, \VAR{b}, and \VAR{c} are all static expressions,
then it is a \emph{static range} of type \EXP{\TYP{StaticRange}\llbracket{}a,n,c\rrbracket}
and therefore also a \emph{range of static size} of type \EXP{\TYP{RangeOfStaticSize}\llbracket{}n\rrbracket}.

\item The range \EXP{a\mathinner{\hbox{\tt\char'43}}n} is the set of
\EXP{\max(0,n)} integers $\{a, a+1, a+2, \ldots, a+n-3, a+n-2, a+n-1\}$.
This is a \emph{nonstrided} range.
If \VAR{a} and \VAR{n} are both static expressions,
then it is a \emph{static range} of type \EXP{\TYP{StaticRange}\llbracket{}a,n,1\rrbracket}
If \VAR{n} is a static expression, then it is a \emph{range of static size}
of type \EXP{\TYP{RangeOfStaticSize}\llbracket{}n\rrbracket},
even if \VAR{a} is not a static expression.
\end{itemize}

The reasoning is in
\nolinkurl{explorations/compile-ladder/rung-walk-instance/decision-record.md}
in the revival's repository.
The order, a declaration chosen and then instantiated, is that of
\secref{resolving-coercion}, read on the parameter types that declarations
declare, as the type group's paper of 2011 reads a declaration with static
parameters: it ``is applicable to a type if and only if at least one of its
instances is'' (\nolinkurl{Papers/Types/setup.tick}, lines 396--397, in the
revival's repository).
The numeral's default is what the interpreter did before this change, giving
a numeral the narrowest of \EXP{\mathbb{Z}32}, \EXP{\mathbb{Z}64} and
nothing at a call fixes whose declared bound and expected type are two traits
that meet at their intersection.
A program that the compiled path ran before this revision, at one conjunct of
such an intersection or at \TYP{BottomType}, now dies loading that instance.
A written bound, such as \TYP{Number}, is taken by both implementations where
the chapter gives it.
Under the interpreter, a type parameter that nothing at a call fixes runs at its
bound where it ran at \TYP{BottomType}, and a type parameter with no narrowest
candidate at its bound where it ran at the arguments' narrowest named common
supertype, except the type parameters that the boxes on the interpreter name;
a call whose arguments have several minimal common supertypes runs where it
stopped the interpreter, unless they fix a type parameter declared with several
bounds that the interpreter cannot meet or one whose bound mentions the type
parameter itself.
\item[Original text] \nolinkurl{Specification-1.0-frozen/basic/inference.tex},
lines 12--27, which held after the chapter's heading two draft notes:
\begin{quote}
This chapter will include the Fortress static type inference mechanism.
\end{quote}
and the note that the chapter keeps:
\begin{quote}
\begin{itemize}
\item There seems to be a circular dependency between inference and
juxtaposition disambiguation -- you have to know if the subexpressions have
arrow types to disambiguate, but you can't do that without using inference,
which requires knowing how the variable of unknown type is used.

data.summary:
One blocking finding: a specification sentence that rung K's code has made false. Everything else that was wrong was in the records, and I fixed it in ecd8fa04a, which touches only explorations/.

**Blocking.** Specification/appendices/changes.tex:1321 still says "The interpreter does not check comprises clauses." Since rung K, walk checks the main component's clauses at load (Driver.java:227, BuildEnvironments.checkComprisesClauses). The gather compared only W's text against K's code, so it missed this older sentence. The repair is one sentence of specification text, so the first gate's tables stand.

**Check 1, batch rules.**
- Rule 1 holds. W and K edit disjoint Java files. In Library/FortressLibrary.fsi and .fss, R's declarations and S's are disjoint: R has Just's SQCAP, OpenRange.narrowToRange, RightRange.leftOrRight, FullRange's IN, the ternary `::` operators and SimpleMappedSeqIndexed. S has the members of the String trait and `reverse`. Test files are distinct.
- Rule 2 holds by reading:
  - K's overlap reading accepts only more sets than before and still calls the three-argument inferByUnification, which W left with the base's behaviour.
  - S's String opr[r0] calls FullRange.narrowToRange, which R did not edit.
  - No test of W, R or S declares a comprises clause.
  - The gate judges the rest.

**Check 2, commit contents.** Each commit carries its edit, tests and records. The one departure is the gather's, and it recorded it: S's commit also carries the re-anchoring of W's rows 589 and 590 and the batch RECORD.md, because amending K's and R's commits was refused.

**Check 3, folded records.**
- Rows 587 to 609 are contiguous and in manifest order. No row was removed or moved. Every changed row only had its notes appended and its status updated. The ledger's counts are a frozen 2026-09-15 derivation, untouched.
- No provisional number is left. The `<short hash>` placeholders remain for the commit stage.
- I corrected stale line citations in two FACTS entries, one false FACTS claim ('Choosing a declaration is unchanged'), and base-line citations in rows 424, 599, 600 and 609 and in PLAN item 40.
- The handover's opening paragraphs (last landing 7b, count 59) were already stale at the base. Updating them is the coordinator's step after landing.

**Check 4, corrections and rows.** All 18 corrections the gather lists are closed, each checked in its file. Every recommended row was opened or refused.

**Check 5, commit messages.** Footers are exact, no model identifier appears, and each commit has a historical: line naming exactly the 2012-tree files it edits.

**Check 6, provenance blocks.** W's and R's historical: lines lacked a file:line; I added them. All four SKEPTIC.md files say the lines were opened.

**Check 7, homes.** One gap: D5's reach, which the second skeptic measured, has no pin and no row. I routed it as review-routed.1 under the D5 entry.

**Check 8, stops.** Seven stops were met, all lifted by POSITIONS.md:100. K met none.
